title: Halves and quarters
examples: Teacher, what does it mean to share something equally?
If I have four cookies, how do I share them between two friends?
Can we draw a pizza and cut it into quarters?

explain.say: Today we are learning how to share things fairly.
To share fairly, you must make sure every piece is the same size.

draw.text: Equal parts are the same size.

explain.say: Let us look at a pizza cut into halves. This means two equal pieces.

draw.text: Pizza cut into halves (2 equal pieces)

explain.say: Now, imagine cutting that pizza into quarters. This means four equal pieces.

draw.text: Pizza cut into quarters (4 equal pieces)

explain.say: If you have four friends, you can give each friend one quarter piece of pizza.
When you share your crayons equally, you are making sure everyone gets the same amount.

faq.q: What is the difference between halves and quarters?
faq.a: Halves mean dividing something into two equal parts. Quarters mean dividing it into four equal parts.
asks: How many pieces are in quarters?
Is a quarter smaller than a half?

faq.q: If I share 6 toys between 2 people, what do I get?
faq.a: You would give each person 3 toys so it is shared equally.
asks: How do I share 6 equally between 2?

faq.q: Do I always have to use halves and quarters?
faq.a: No, you can share things into three equal parts, which we call thirds.
asks: Can I share into three parts?
What if I share into six parts?

faq.q: What does 'equal parts' mean when we share?
faq.a: It means every single piece must be exactly the same size as every other piece.
asks: How do I make sure the parts are the same?

faq.q: If I cut a cake into quarters, what do I get?
faq.a: You get four pieces, and each piece is one quarter of the whole cake.
asks: How many pieces are in quarters?

facts: Halves mean dividing something into 2 equal parts.
Quarters mean dividing something into 4 equal parts.
Sharing fairly always means making equal parts.
Four quarters fit together to make one whole.

quiz.say: If you share 1 whole chocolate bar equally between 2 friends, each friend gets:
quiz.why: Sharing between two people always gives you halves.

wrong.0: This means you gave them two pieces, which is too much.
wrong.2: This would mean you only gave them one small piece.
wrong.3: This would mean only one person got the chocolate bar.

quiz.say: If a circle is cut into 4 equal pieces, each piece is called:

wrong.0: A whole is all the pieces put back together.
wrong.1: We use one word to describe the size of the piece.
wrong.3: A half is only two equal pieces.

quiz.say: If you share 4 stickers equally between 2 friends, how many does each get?
quiz.why: Four divided by two equals two.

wrong.1: This is like counting the stickers twice.
wrong.2: This means only one friend got a sticker.
wrong.3: This means no sharing happened at all.
